blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how to predict the efficiency of an algorithm without running it? Understanding the complexity of loops and recursion is key to this prediction.

blocks.markdown: In this lesson, we will explore how to analyze the time complexity of algorithms, focusing on nested loops and recursive functions. By the end of this lesson, you will be able to derive the time complexity from loop bounds and solve recurrences for divide-and-conquer algorithms.

blocks.title: Time Complexity
blocks.text: Time complexity is a computational complexity that describes the amount of time it takes to run an algorithm as a function of the length of the input.

blocks.markdown:
### Analysing Nested Loops
Nested loops are common in algorithms, and understanding their time complexity is crucial. The time complexity of nested loops is determined by the number of iterations each loop performs.

blocks.title: Example: Nested Loops

steps.text: The outer loop runs from 1 to n, which means it executes n times.
For each iteration of the outer loop, the inner loop also runs from 1 to n, executing n times.
Thus, the total number of operations is the product of the two loops: $n \times n = n^2$.

blocks.answer: The time complexity of the nested loops is $O(n^2)$.

blocks.markdown:
### Analysing Recursion
Recursive algorithms often have a time complexity that can be expressed as a recurrence relation. Solving this recurrence helps us understand the algorithm's efficiency.

blocks.title: Recurrence Relation
blocks.text: A recurrence relation is an equation that recursively defines a sequence, where the next term is a function of the previous terms.

blocks.title: Example: Recursive Algorithm

steps.text: The function calls itself twice for each call with $n > 1$. This suggests a recurrence relation of the form $T(n) = 2T(n-1) + c$, where $c$ is a constant.
Solving this recurrence using the Master Theorem or expansion gives $T(n) = O(2^n)$.

blocks.answer: The time complexity of the recursive function is $O(2^n)$.

blocks.markdown:
### Space Complexity of Recursive Algorithms
Space complexity refers to the amount of memory space required by an algorithm. Recursive algorithms often have additional space complexity due to the call stack.

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.text: The space complexity of a recursive algorithm is often determined by the maximum depth of the recursion.

points: Nested loops' time complexity is derived from the product of the loop bounds.
Recurrence relations describe the time complexity of recursive algorithms.
Space complexity in recursion is influenced by the call stack depth.
